attributes.law_screen: claim.law.point-of-use-single-use-pointer-delay APPLIED IN REVERSE and was decisive: hoisting `handle = mgr + region*4` above the __shl2i call (axis 1) REGRESSED real 8 -> 45 and dropped an addi (83 -> 82 insns), proving the target's `add` must stay at point of use while only the `slwi` is hoisted. claim.law.pointer-reassociation-controls-add-operand-order screened, NOT applicable: both streams already emit base-first (`add rD,r31,r0`), the divergence was the destination register only. claim.law.direct-global-member-flips-index-base-association APPLIED: spelling the site as a member of the direct global lbl_802C7438 instead of via the local `mgr` alias flipped the index/base association and took real 8 -> 0. claim.law.local-alias-vs-direct-global-spelling-diverges APPLIED (same mechanism, confirms the local-alias vs direct-global split). claim.law.sizeof-defeats-loop-stride-induction screened, not applicable (no sizeof stride at this site). claim.law.lwzu-idiom-web-retention screened, not applicable (no load-update idiom in this web).
attributes.residual: Instruction stream byte-identical (probe real 0, fndiff --ops IDENTICAL 83/83). fndiff --clean still prints 8 lines, ALL of them the relocation SPELLING of one 64-bit global's low half: ours emits `lbl_803450D8+0x4` / `lbl_803450E0+0x4` where the target names `lbl_803450DC` / `lbl_803450E4`. config/GUNE5D/symbols.txt declares four separate 4-byte .sbss objects at 0x803450D8/DC/E0/E4 while pb_texture.c declares two `u64`s covering the same eight bytes; lbl_803450D8+4 == lbl_803450DC == 0x803450DC, so the EMB_SDA21 displacement encodes identically and the emitted bytes are equal. The u64 typing is semantically correct (0x2f regions needs a >32-bit mask; __shl2i is a genuine 64-bit shift), so this is a verified symbol-name normalization, not a codegen gap. See claim.law.u64-global-spanning-two-symbol-labels-spells-plus-four.
